pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - Bishop John Robinson C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
At our school, Collective Worship is the heartbeat of our day, centred on our Core Christian Values of Trust, Forgiveness, and Compassion. However, our exploration of faith extends far beyond these three. We follow a comprehensive termly cycle that introduces students to a wide range of additional values, ensuring they develop a holistic understanding of Christian character and how to live well in community (Oikoumene).
Our Weekly Worship Cycle
Each value—whether a core or seasonal focus—is explored through a consistent weekly structure:
Extended Values and Themes
While Trust, Forgiveness, and Compassion are our foundation, we also dedicate specific terms to values such as:
Inclusive and Inspirational Worship
Worship includes everyone from Reception to Year 6, with tailored support for pupils with Special Educational Needs. Our sessions are frequently enriched by inspirational visitors, who model these values in various walks of life.
Through the use of liturgical traditions—such as seasonal colours and varied Bible translations—pupils gain a deep understanding of the Trinitarian nature of God (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit) and the importance of personal reflection.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Values - Bishop John Robinson C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Our vision is for all children and adults to;
Be the best they can;
Join in Learning, Play and Prayer,
Remember God's Word
At Bishop John Robinson CofE Primary School, our identity, curriculum, and spiritual ethos are anchored in our faith: “Jesus is the anchor of my soul” (Hebrews 6:19).
We empower adults and children alike to achieve their divine potential, securing the best possible start in life and multiplying the gifts God has given them.
The Five Anchors of Our Faith and Learning
“Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart.” — Colossians 3:23
We cultivate an environment of high aspirations and unbroken focus. We achieve this by:
“Instruct us in the way of knowledge and wisdom and lead us along straight paths.” — Proverbs 4:11
We inspire a lifelong love for education, driving academic excellence that impacts wider society. We achieve this by:
“Do to others as you would have them do to you.” — Luke 6:31
Play is the heartbeat of social and emotional growth at BJR. Through positive play, children learn to trust, forgive, and build resilience. We achieve this by:
“Be joyful. Never stop praying. Whatever happens, give thanks.” — 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18
Prayer builds our personal relationship with God. It anchors our community in gratitude and praise. We achieve this by:
“Train up a child in the way they should go, and when they are old they will not depart from it.” — Proverbs 22:6
Scripture is our foundation. We bring Christian values to life through practical, daily application. We achieve this by:
Gathering for inspiring, high-quality collective worship.
Our Values in Action
We explore these three anchor values daily through collective worship, classroom reflection times, and restorative justice practices. They shape our school policies and dictate how we treat one another.
Living the Values Daily
Class Names as Identity: Every year group champions a distinct Christian value. Your child will journey through these values as they grow:
Celebrating Success: We actively spot and reward children who demonstrate these values through their hard work and choices.
British Values: We seamlessly interweave Fundamental British Values alongside our Christian teachings to prepare children for life in modern Britain.
Religious Education is a core subject at Bishop John Robinson Church of England Primary School and plays a central role in our curriculum and the life of our school. As a Church of England school, our provision is rooted in our Christian vision and values, enabling pupils to develop a deep understanding of Christianity while fostering respect, curiosity and appreciation for other faiths and worldviews.
Our commitment to providing a rich and meaningful Christian education was recognised in our 2023 Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS), where the school was judged excellent. This reflects our dedication to ensuring that our Christian vision is lived out through every aspect of school life, including the high-quality provision for Religious Education.
Through engaging and thought-provoking learning, pupils are encouraged to ask challenging questions, reflect on life's big issues, and explore their own beliefs and values alongside those of others. They develop the knowledge, skills and understanding needed to think critically, appreciate different perspectives, and demonstrate empathy, compassion and respect in an increasingly diverse society.
Our approach to Religious Education extends well beyond discrete lessons. Opportunities to explore spiritual, moral, ethical and cultural themes are woven throughout the curriculum, collective worship and the wider life of the school. Pupils are encouraged to make meaningful connections between their learning, their own experiences and the wider world, helping them to become reflective, responsible and compassionate citizens.
Religious Education makes a significant contribution to pupils' spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. It equips them with the confidence to engage thoughtfully with questions of faith and belief, celebrates diversity, promotes mutual respect, and prepares them to flourish academically, spiritually and personally within our school community and beyond

Year 6: Justice

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Faith - Bishop John Robinson C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Faith
Welcome to the heart of our school community! This corner of our website is a place to celebrate what makes us truly unique—our Christian Distinctiveness. For us, faith is not just a subject; it’s the golden thread that runs through everything we do.
We invite you to explore the links on the left to discover the vibrant world of Collective Worship and the deep, cherished bonds we share with our local church. By clicking through, you can see how our daily life is shaped by our core values of trust, forgiveness and compassion, alongside the many other virtues we explore together.
What You’ll Discover:
Whether you are a current parent, a prospective family, or a visitor, we hope these pages give you a real sense of the warmth, prayer, and reflection that define our school family.
Church Links - St Paul's Church Thamesmead
St Paul’s United Church in Thamesmead is our school church, and we are proud of our close and caring partnership. Reverend Patrick Eggleston, who serves as the church incumbent and also as our Chair of Governors, plays an active role in the spiritual life of our school.
We celebrate our key Christian festivals together, with services held both in school and at St Paul’s throughout the year. These shared celebrations help our pupils grow in faith, reflect on Christian values, and feel part of a wider worshipping community.
Our relationship with St Paul’s is an important part of our identity as a Church of England school, enriching the experiences of our pupils and supporting their spiritual development.
For up-to-date information about their services, please visit the Southwark Diocese website: https://southwark.anglican.org/find-a-church/plumstead/thamesmead-team-ministry/thamesmead-st-paul

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Head Teacher - Bishop John Robinson C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head Teacher
A very warm welcome to Bishop John Robinson, a one-form entry Church of England primary school in the heart of Thamesmead.
We are proud of our joyful, caring, and inclusive school community where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to be the best they can be. Our school vision—Be the best we can, join in learning, play and prayer, and remember God’s word—is at the heart of everything we do. It shapes our understanding, our relationships, and the way we live and grow together each day.
Our core Christian values of trust, forgiveness, and compassion guide every aspect of school life. They help us to build strong relationships, nurture character, and create a safe and respectful environment where all children can thrive.
While we are rooted in our Christian foundation, we warmly welcome children of the Christian faith, those of other faiths, and those with no faith. We celebrate the unique qualities of every child and the rich diversity that reflects our vibrant Thamesmead community.
Alongside our strong spiritual and moral foundation, we are deeply committed to academic excellence.
Through a broad, engaging, and ambitious curriculum, we challenge and inspire our pupils—equipping them with the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need to succeed now and in the future.
Great importance is placed on the partnership between home and school, working closely with parents and carers to build strong, supportive relationships. Through open communication, engaging workshops, and shared events, we foster a collaborative community where everyone feels valued, involved, and empowered. By supporting families, we help to create a connected, thriving environment where every child—and the wider school community—can flourish.
Thank you for taking the time to explore our website. We are incredibly proud of our pupils and all that we achieve together at Bishop John Robinson. If you’d like to learn more, please do get in touch—we would be delighted to welcome you in person.
Sarah Biney

Inspection Reports
At Bishop John Robinson, our vision anchors everything we do, creating an environment where children and staff truly flourish.
We are incredibly proud that our commitment to academic excellence, pastoral care, and deep-rooted Christian values are consistently recognised by national inspection bodies.
Under the rigorous new framework, our 2023 SIAMS inspection graded our school 'EXCELLENT' in all areas. This extraordinary achievement stands alongside a decade of sustained academic standards, validated by three consecutive 'GOOD' ratings from OFSTED in 2014, 2018, and 2024. Enhanced by our Primary Science Quality Mark, these reports reflect a joyful, high-achieving community where curiosity is nurtured and every child is supported to be the very best they can be.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND and Inclusion - Bishop John Robinson C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion
Sustained improvement, meaningful progress and equal opportunities for all pupils underpin every aspect of learning and strengthen our school’s inclusive ethos.
At Bishop John Robinson C of E Primary School, we welcome children with special educational and additional needs, including those with disabilities.
The progress of our children is regularly monitored by teachers with needs identified promptly and discussed with our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO), Mrs Hayleigh Ijagbone, and the parents concerned. Parental engagement and support in meeting children’s educational needs is vital if all children are to reach their potential.
Being an inclusive school, we are proud of the extra provision we offer our pupils with special educational and additional needs. The Inclusion Lead and Senior Leadership Team meet with parents to discuss how best we can support their child's needs, through in-school interventions and provision, as well as benefiting from the advice and expertise of external agencies. Please see information about Grace Class below.
Most support is given within the class through planned support from the teacher and working in small groups with a member of our support staff. Specialist help may be given through withdrawal and individual support. We may also refer to outside agencies with specialised knowledge.
If you have concerns about your child and think they may be experiencing difficulty with their learning, please feel free to discuss this with the class teacher or contact the Special Needs Co-ordinator on the school telephone number.
For information about the Royal Borough of Greenwich's Local Offer, please click on the link below:
https://greenwichcommunitydirectory.org.uk/children-young-people-additional-needs
Our SEN Policies are available to read or download from our Policies Page
Grace Class
“I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.” — John 10:10
Welcome to Grace Class, our specialist School-Based Resourced Provision. We provide high-quality, expert support for pupils with complex Communication and Interaction needs, including Speech, Language and Communication Needs (SLCN), and Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs.
Guided by our Christian ethos, we look at every single child through the lens of God's love. We believe that every child is uniquely made, every child belongs, and every child can flourish. Our ultimate aim is to create an environment where all pupils truly enjoy their school life and achieve their full potential through the right relationships, expert teaching, and bespoke support.
Our Vision & the Grace Way
Our vision is to create a specialist learning environment where every pupil feels completely safe, deeply understood, and fully empowered. Through high expectations, evidence-informed practices, and a close partnership with families, we nurture confident communicators, resilient learners, and independent young people ready for the world.
In Grace Class, every step forward matters. Whether a child is speaking their first functional word, joining a group activity, managing a routine independently, or achieving academic excellence, we celebrate it all.
How We Walk "The Grace Way"
Relationships before Expectations: We establish trust, safety, and mutual respect first.
Enjoyment & Achievement: We design learning to be engaging, ensuring children love coming to school while reaching ambitious milestones.
Behaviour as Communication: We understand that every child has a voice, and behaviour is a form of communication that we meet with empathy.
High Support & High Expectations: We provide the scaffolded support needed so that no ceiling is placed on a child's aspirations.
Faith & Family Partnerships: We walk alongside our families and community, working hand-in-hand to support our children.
Our Core GRACE Values
Our values are the heartbeat of our provision, reflecting both our curriculum intent and our Christian character:
Grow: Every child can make progress from their individual starting point.
Respect: We value ourselves, others, and our community as unique individuals.
Aspire: We maintain ambitious, hopeful expectations for every single learner.
Communicate: Every voice matters, and every child has a right to be heard and understood.
Empower: We purposefully develop independence, inner confidence, and lifelong resilience.
The Learning Environment
To help children focus, enjoy, and achieve, our learning environment is intentionally calm, predictable, and low-arousal. Our spaces are carefully designed to reduce sensory overload and optimize engagement, featuring:
Whole-class direct teaching zones
Small-group collaborative learning spaces
Distraction-free individual workstations
A dedicated sensory regulation area
Tailored communication resources (including visual schedules and boards)
Our Six Foundations Curriculum
The Grace Class curriculum beautifully complements the National Curriculum. It explicitly teaches the vital communication, emotional regulation, and independence skills that allow children to succeed both in school and the wider community.
Our curriculum focuses on six core areas, enriched by specialist, evidence-based interventions:
1. Communication and Interaction
2. Emotional Regulation and Wellbeing
3. Cognition and Learning
4. Independence and Life Skills
5. Physical and Sensory
6. Social Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding - Bishop John Robinson C.E. Primary School
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
At Bishop John Robinson Church of England Primary School, the health, safety and well-being of children is of paramount concern to us. We listen to our pupils and take seriously what they tell us. Our aim is for children to enjoy their time as pupils in this school.
We want to work in partnership with you to help your child achieve their full potential and make a positive contribution to the world they are part of.
Our policies relating to safeguarding apply to all adults, including volunteers working in or on behalf of the school. To promote a safe environment for pupils, our selection and recruitment policy includes all checks on staff and regular volunteers’ suitability, including Disclosure and Barring Service checks.
The school's Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) is Ms Sarah Biney, supported by Mr Michael Elegbede and Miss Sara Pazola. Our designated Governors are Mrs Susan Robinson and Mrs Abigail Asiedu.
All have received appropriate and up-to-date training for this role. It is their responsibility to ensure that all staff in contact with children receive child protection awareness training on a regular basis.
We are committed to establishing and maintaining an ethos where children feel safe, secure, valued and respected, and are encouraged to talk openly and are always listened to and ensuring that all children know there is an adult in school whom they can approach if they are worried or in difficulty, including opportunities in the wider curriculum for children to develop the skills they need to recognise and stay safe from harm.
The staff are aware that it is their responsibility to be alert to signs of abuse and to follow the procedures set out in the school’s Safeguarding Policy. Occasions arise when our concern about a child requires us to consult other agencies. Whilst we would always aim to work in partnership with parents, there may be exceptions to this when concerns are raised about the protection of a child. The role of the school in situations where there are child protection concerns is not to investigate but to recognise and refer. On very rare occasions, representatives from Children’s Social Care or the police may want to speak to a child or parent. This would be a decision made in collaboration with partner agencies and would only be done in situations where a child might be at immediate risk.
We will always take advice from the Local Safeguarding Children’s Board and follow their procedures when required. If you want to know more about our procedures, please speak to the Headteacher. Please see our policies page for our safeguarding policy.

Early Years Foundation Stage
EYFS Curriculum Vision and Intent
In the Early Years and Foundation Stage, our vision is to provide a high-quality, nurturing, and inspiring start to every child’s educational journey. We aim to establish a strong foundation for both academic achievement and moral and spiritual growth, enabling children to thrive as confident, curious, and lifelong learners.
Our EYFS provision ensures that all children make strong progress from their individual starting points through child-led, purposeful play, high-quality teaching, and consistent assessment. Practice reflects the BJR teaching and learning approach, with a clear emphasis on early reading, communication, language, writing, and mathematics, ensuring every child develops the essential skills and knowledge to succeed.
We believe that play is central to all learning in EYFS. Through child-initiated exploration, children develop independence, creativity, and resilience. Strong, purposeful adult interactions extend learning, challenge thinking, and model language, while supporting the development of oracy skills—enabling children to communicate effectively, articulate ideas, collaborate, and problem-solve.
We foster the right learning habits through the Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning: Play, Exploration, Active Learning, Creativity, and Critical Thinking. Our continuous provision is ambitious, inclusive, and responsive to children’s needs, offering rich, engaging, and meaningful experiences across indoor and outdoor environments. This is enhanced through trips, visits, and regular forest school sessions, which stimulate curiosity, wonder, and discovery.
At our school, EYFS is more than preparing children academically; it is about holistic development, ensuring children flourish socially, emotionally, morally, and spiritually. By combining high expectations, purposeful play, child-led exploration, and intentional adult support, we aim to ignite a lifelong passion for learning and growth, equipping children to become thoughtful, creative and engaged members of society.

Mathematics
At BJR, we aim to inspire a lifelong love of learning in mathematics by developing confident, curious and resilient learners who demonstrate positive attitudes towards challenge. Through a carefully structured curriculum, we ensure all children develop strong foundations in mathematical knowledge and skills, enabling them to build upon knowledge as they progress.
Grounded in our Christian values of forgiveness, compassion and trust, our mathematics curriculum promotes perseverance, collaboration and respect. Children are encouraged to learn from mistakes, show compassion towards others and trust in their own ability to succeed. Mathematics learning is enriched through meaningful links to our faith and a strong connection with our community, ensuring relevance and purpose.
Using the White Rose Maths Scheme, we provide a coherent, mastery-based curriculum that enables all pupils to achieve depth of understanding and confidence in mathematics.
Maths – Implementation
Mathematics is taught daily using the White Rose Maths Scheme, ensuring clear progression and consistency across all year groups. Teaching is underpinned by Rosenshine’s Principles of Instruction, which support effective learning and long-term retention.
Lessons include hands-on activities using concrete and pictorial resources to engage and enthuse children, ensuring learning is accessible to all. Teachers regularly adapt teaching in response to assessment, providing timely intervention, additional challenge or alternative representations where needed.
A key focus is placed on addressing misconceptions. Misunderstandings are anticipated through careful planning and tackled through targeted questioning, live marking, and responsive teaching, ensuring all pupils develop secure understanding before moving on.
Classroom environments promote confidence and trust, where mistakes are valued as learning opportunities, reflecting our commitment to forgiveness and compassion.

pageCache.text:
Phonics & Reading
We have a whole school commitment to making sure that every child is able to read and read confidently. We want our children to become enthusiastic, engaged readers and to develop a life-long love of books. We introduce children to a range of high-quality fiction, non-fiction and poetry books through our whole-class, core-text approach to teaching reading, and during their daily whole-class reading lessons.
In the early stages of reading, we teach children to decode words using phonic skills. Once grasped, the focus for developing reading is understanding and comprehension. During whole-class reading sessions, pupils are encouraged to consider what a ‘good reader’ is and the skills that are required to be able to not only decode words but read for meaning and pleasure. At Bishop John Robinson, we know that ‘good readers’ use a number of skills at once and therefore lessons are carefully planned to include opportunities for pupils to identify and practise these with others before applying them independently.
Pupils are also given opportunities to read for pleasure outside of lessons. Every class visits our local library every term to spend time selecting their own books to add to the classroom library. When the pupils have finished their chosen book, they swap with others. We also have our whole school ‘book swap’ areas where pupils are free to choose any book they like to take home and read. This could mean that pupils are revisiting old favourites or choosing books about specific subjects that are not on their current curriculum. Pupils across the school are eager to share their passion for reading during whole school worship where each class has the opportunity to recommend a ‘book of the week’.
At BJR we encourage children to read daily and to discuss the books they have taken home. All children will bring home a levelled reader from the Oxford University Press reading scheme and an additional book of their choosing for pleasure. Levelled readers will be changed weekly where children can read and discuss the book confidently and children will be encouraged to change their reading for pleasure book regularly.
Parental support is hugely important for developing their reading skills, confidence and understanding. Even if your child is an independent reader, it is still important for you to read with them, listen to them and discuss the books they are reading.
What will my child experience?
Learning to read has a high emphasis in all classes, especially in our Early Years and Key Stage 1 classrooms. Daily whole-class phonic sessions take place in which children are taught phonemes and the ability to blend in order for them to develop into fluent readers. Children initially take home a free-choice book which is changed every week. This book should be read/shared by an adult. At the beginning of the Spring Term, children also take home a levelled book which the child should read to someone. Both books are changed once per week.
Every child reads to the Class Teacher 1:1 once per week and a record is made in the Reading Record to inform parents of any observations or next steps. Reading records are checked weekly and parent comments are acknowledged. Children are to read several times per week through whole-class Literacy sessions, where we have a book focus for a period of time, and we often finish the day with story-time.
Every child will bring home a levelled book from The Oxford University Press. Levelled books are changed and sent home weekly. We aim to listen to each child read individually in school every week. Children have reading records that accompany their home books which the parent/carers complete.
Children in Year 2 will begin whole-class reading lessons using the ‘Routes to reading’ scheme, which builds on our phonics scheme.

Religious Education
RE is Excellent at BJR!
At Bishop John Robinson, Religious Education (RE) is the "core of the core" curriculum, central to our distinctive Christian character. Our intent is to provide a high-quality, inclusive RE curriculum from EYFS to Year 6 that enables every child to flourish and live "life in all its fullness" (John 10:10).
We follow the Southwark Diocesan Board of Education (SDBE) RE Syllabus. This framework ensures a progressive and sequential journey of "religious literacy," where children develop the skills of enquiry, analysis and reflection.
To ensure our pupils are prepared for life in a diverse and global society, our curriculum is broad and balanced. While Christianity is taught as a core religion in every year group, we also provide a systematic and in-depth study of the other main world religions:
In EYFS, children begin by exploring their own experiences and special places. As they progress through Key Stages 1 and 2, they move from identifying the beliefs and practices of these six faiths to analysing how these beliefs impact the way people live their lives today.
Our RE curriculum is the primary vehicle for embedding our school’s core Christian values:
Trust: We create a safe space for "Big Questions," where children trust that their unique beliefs and questions of meaning will be heard and respected.
Compassion: By learning about the lives and traditions of the six main world religions, our pupils develop empathy and a drive to "stand in someone else’s shoes," reflecting the love and kindness of Jesus.
Forgiveness: Through the study of Biblical narratives and the "Salvation" story, children understand that mistakes are part of the human journey and that reconciliation is key to a flourishing community.
Local Church and Community Links
Our RE is not confined to the classroom. We maintain a vital, living link with our school parish, St Paul’s Church, which serves as a spiritual "second home" for our school. Pupils visit the church throughout the year to celebrate Christian festivals such as Christmas and Easter and our school Reverend, Patrick Eggleston, visits us regularly, supporting our RE delivery and leading Collective Worship.
By the end of Year 6, our pupils will be religiously literate citizens who can hold balanced and well-informed conversations about religion and belief. They leave us equipped with the "disciplinary lenses"—theological, philosophical, and sociological—needed to navigate a diverse world with confidence and grace.
While we believe our inclusive RE curriculum is vital for helping children understand the diverse world they live in, we respect that parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education lessons. If you are considering this, we encourage you to speak with the Headteacher so we can share our syllabus with you and discuss how your child’s needs can be best met during these times.
